title: The Non-Returnees
subtitle:
The darkness cuts their shadows from their heels.
And at that empty door, their families mourn the whole night long.

content.text: Heavy rain will eventually cause a flood. It's an obvious deduction.
This is my final report. The era of mankind and birds is over, and the era of fish has begun.
But the fish will have to wait a little longer. Because you've delayed the doomsday by about an hour.
Every living person now owes you an hour of their lives. How big do you think your medal should be?

branch.text: Certainly. Even if the umbrellas don't work, you still have an ark.
Just as long as you only take the "qualified animals" with you, like in old times ...
You should be able to continue to fight.
Please, let me finish my final report, even if you don't want to hear it.
Thanks to gravity, those on higher ground live longer in a flood.
Which gives you plenty of time to cuddle up with your greyhound and watch the end of the world together.
Or ... you could do what a soldier would and follow your orders till the very last moment.
You know how important this mission is.

items.text: Outside the carriage come heavy footsteps, followed by a wave of restless complaints.
The Extra Carriage

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: You hear that? Boots. Sounds like soldiers.

items.speaker: Reyhan
items.text: Could it be Pyrrhos again?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Pyrrhos?

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: An army officer. He's working with the conductress to get us out of here.
A new name, a new problem.
Semmelweis frowns.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Come on, Rubuska. Time to go.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Huh? Oh, right! I'm supposed to be in Aima's cabin. I better not be seen here.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: W-Wait! Ms. Rubuska!
Just about to leave, she turns back to face the boy.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: Th-Thank you for protecting us. I-I hope I can be brave like you when I grow up.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: You're a good vampire!
She can't help but smile as she leans down to pat his head.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: And you're a good boy, Ivanushka.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Now listen, this good vampire has to go up front for a bit. But I'll be back soon with news from the other carriages.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: No one will hurt you, you got that? Not while I'm around. Here, pinky promise.
She reaches out her right hand to Ivanushka, hooking her pinky.
So Ivanushka lifts his good hand, pinky finger locking with hers.
Their promise is sealed.

items.speaker: Ivanushka
items.text: I'll be waiting for you. You promised, so come back soon, Rubuska.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Don't worry, I will. Look, I'll take this.
She picks up the wooden stake at her feet and gives it a little shake.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: As a token of our promise. So you better hold the fort for me until I bring it back, alright?
Seating Carriage

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, please bear with us while we conduct a routine check.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: A-Are you going to take us too? Like you did with Rubuska?

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: You give her back right now! Or I'll ... I'll lie down right here! I-I'll be an unmovable object!
The boy flings himself to the ground, clenching his pudgy fists like a martyr ready to face his fate.
It's his final card to play, a tactic that has worked on the adults before, and one that he's counting on to work now.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: If you are set on being "unmovable," I'd be happy to stitch you into the carpet.
He swallows hard.

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: I-I'm not moving! Not until Rubuska's back!

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Another search? Again?

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: I suppose you can never be too sure whether someone's transformed into a beast over lunchtime.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: We're ever so sorry for the inconvenience, but this is for your safety; we just have to check whether ...

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: Oh, I have something to "check" too, young lady. Namely, whether anyone on this crew actually has a brain knocking around in their heads!

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: You say this is for our safety, but all you've done is stir up chaos. You ought to be ashamed!
The carriage is in chaos.
People leave their seats, crowding and shouting. The tension seems about to erupt into fresh turmoil.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: That's quite enough commotion, everyone.
The officer slides his pistol back into his belt as if it were nothing more than a pen—just a tool.
In the uneasy silence, another sound breaks through.
Hrrrk ... Urrrgh ... Rkkk ...
A slow, irregular churning, like the rumbling stomach of some terrible creature.
The noise dips, then rises again into a catlike whimper.
*wail*
All eyes turn toward the pale-faced gentleman in the corner.

items.speaker: Arbuthnot
items.text: I ... W-What're you all starin' for?

items.speaker: Arbuthnot
items.text: That weren't me.
Footsteps echo.
Semmelweis strides through the gathered people at a quick pace, with Rubuska trailing close behind.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: What are you two doing here?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Please, allow me through. There's something wrong.
She moves as she speaks, grabbing Arbuthnot's wrist and yanking it away.

items.speaker: Arbuthnot
items.text: Watch it! I told you, it weren't me.
She shoves him aside and looks at the slumped stranger hiding behind him.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Who are you? I didn't see you during the registration.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Can you speak, sir?
The passenger can hardly lift his face to meet hers.
His face is chalk-white. Red streaks score outward from his pupils.
Then he opens his mouth, revealing a thick, black sea of blood swirling inside.

items.speaker: Unwell Passenger
items.text: Chk ... Chklga—

items.speaker: Passengers
items.text: AAAAHHHH!

items.speaker: Unwell Passenger
items.text: H-Help ...
He collapses, choking on the blood, gurgling as he swallows it back down.
The investigator kneels and pries open his eyelids.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: An Infected?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But this looks nothing like the usual symptoms. A mutation, perhaps?

items.speaker: Passenger III
items.text: Hold on! Hold on! Would anyone care to explain this? What's an Infected? Infected by what?

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: A pinch of cold, a dash of salmonella, and a spoonful of tuberculosis—what do you think?

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: He's been bitten by a vampire.

items.speaker: Passenger III
items.text: Va-Vampire?!
Overwhelmed with shock, the passenger faints.

items.speaker: Passenger I
items.text: My goodness. A vampire? On this train? I figured those were just old stories.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: Oh, dear. Looks like we've got an unwelcome guest aboard. Iglika, did that strange girl do this?
He looks toward Rubuska.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: I overheard the children talking about some shadowless "vampire boss."

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: Oh my. I thought it was just a silly game!
Everyone turns to Rubuska in a convicting silence. Without her hat, there is no hiding those ruby eyes.
Their fears find a cause.

items.speaker: Passenger IV
items.text: I knew there was something wrong with her the moment she came on board. All that shouting and running about.

items.speaker: Passenger II
items.text: And look, she's awfully pale, too.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: No. No, it wasn't me.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: This isn't a courtroom; there's no use pleading your case. You're going to have to leave the train.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: After all, we can't have a vampire wandering free on a train full of ordinary people now, can we?

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: You'll have to find your next bite elsewhere, kid.
Pyrrhos signals to his men.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: Take her away.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Yes, sir.
Heavy boots stomp closer as two soldiers seize Rubuska by the arms.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Don't touch me, ah! Let me go! You've got it all wrong!

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: She said: Don't touch her!
In the next instant, several children rush from the crowd, tugging at the soldiers and shouting.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Please, sir, please listen! Maybe it's a mistake!

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Hey, back off! Whose kids are these? They're interfering with a military operation!
One soldier raises his rifle in irritation.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: They're with me! For crying out loud, you two, come back here!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Annabelle! This is grown-up stuff, okay? You've got to stay out of it!
The children don't budge. Annabelle clutches a coat hem, looking up at Rubuska in panic.
In all the chaos, hers is the only face sharp and clear.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Run, boss!

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Run, Buska.
The air reeks of gunpowder.
No one is hurt, but a jagged dent scars the ceiling.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Last warning! Where are your parents?

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Argh!
In the chaos, a small figure breaks free and hurls herself at the soldier.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: No! Boss—Rubuska!
Rubuska locks onto his arm, her fangs sinking deep into his skin, sucking as if to drain every drop from him.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: *muffled* Put it down!
